searchText: Got this error from geth when running teku: ``` WARN [02-23|10:01:59.040] Served engine_newPayloadV1 conn=127.0.0.1:58926 reqid=60425 duration="120.75µs" err="invalid argument 0: json: cannot unmarshal hex string \"0x\" into Go struct field ExecutableDataV1.baseFeePerGas of type *hexutil.Big" ``` This is that fun case where RLP strips all leading zeros so would send 0x for 0 but JSON-RPC would always use 0x0 right? It's still following the chain fine though so I'm guessing the block really was invalid because base fee shouldn't be 0. Is the fuzzer running on merge-devnet-4? Yes, the fuzzer is running on keys in range 10k-13k Cross posting from <#692062809701482577> : Kiln Spec v2 is now available! 🔥🧱 It comes with the following major updates: - Engine API Auth - `engine_exchangeTransitionConfigurationV1` - EIP-4399: Rename `RANDOM` to `PREVRANDAO` Change set: https://hackmd.io/@n0ble/kiln-spec#v2-change-set Thank you. then devnet which use `klin` meta spec will be able to use like as `kintsugi` testnet? Yes you can use it like kintsugi. The difference is only in the interface between the EL and CL Thank you . And I think that still specifications are not settle yet. When these will be finalized? That sounds like baseFeePErGas was actually null/nil, not `0`. A byte w/ value `0x00` should be encoded as `0x80` in RLP, I _think_ in this case a "null byte pointer" would get encoded as the empty list `0xc0`. edit: or at least this sounds related to the fact that Geth's ExecutableDataV1.BaseFeePerGas data type is `*big.Int` rather than `big.Int`. Oh wait, I see, it sounds like teku passed in `baseFeePerGas: 0x` in the passed-in JSON when it probably should have passed in `0x0`. > that fun case where RLP strips all leading zeros For the JSONRPC encoding of `QUANTITY` only the _first_ leading zero (if it exists) should be stripped. So `0x00 -> 0x0`, `0x01 -> 0x1` etc. I'm unclear where the canonical encoding description for JSONRPC types is these days, but I think it's here: https://eth.wiki/json-rpc/API (under `HEX value encoding`). edit: ok, I guess `0x0001` still becomes `0x1` so a more correct description of the rule is "after removing any leading 0-value bytes remove the first leading zero if it exists of the hexadecimal representation". When updating to the Kiln Spec v2, will all Execution clients use 8550 port for JWT authenticated http requests or will any client use a different port number? We use 8550 got http, 8551 for ws

WARN [02-23|10:01:59.040] Served engine_newPayloadV1               conn=127.0.0.1:58926 reqid=60425                   duration="120.75µs"  err="invalid argument 0: json: cannot unmarshal hex string \"0x\" into Go struct field ExecutableDataV1.baseFeePerGas of type *hexutil.Big"

This is that fun case where RLP strips all leading zeros so would send 0x for 0 but JSON-RPC would always use 0x0 right?

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content:
That sounds like baseFeePErGas was actually null/nil, not `0`.  A byte w/ value `0x00` should be encoded as `0x80` in RLP, I _think_ in this case a "null byte pointer" would get encoded as the empty list `0xc0`.

edit: or at least this sounds related to the fact that Geth's ExecutableDataV1.BaseFeePerGas data type is `*big.Int`  rather than `big.Int`.

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content:
Oh wait, I see, it sounds like teku passed in `baseFeePerGas: 0x` in the passed-in JSON when it probably should have passed in `0x0`.  

> that fun case where RLP strips all leading zeros

For the JSONRPC encoding of `QUANTITY` only the _first_ leading zero (if it exists) should be stripped.  So `0x00 -> 0x0`, `0x01 -> 0x1` etc.  I'm unclear where the canonical encoding description for JSONRPC types is these days, but I think it's here: https://eth.wiki/json-rpc/API (under `HEX value encoding`).

edit: ok, I guess `0x0001` still becomes `0x1` so a more correct description of the rule is "after removing any leading 0-value bytes remove the first leading zero if it exists of the hexadecimal representation".
